EditorsHub is a work in progress
This build is still an early release. Some features are limited and you may run into occasional bugs.
playback, the timeline, the 3D system, performance and other editing features

EditorsHub grows step by step, focused on becoming a flexible, lightweight motion graphics editor with a comfortable workflow.
EditorsHub is built on the open-source Open Motion engine, which is still evolving quickly, so new features, fixes and workflow improvements arrive with every update.
native build: the editor runs on your device, works offline, and exports straight to your gallery or the share sheet.
What is the Open Motion engine?
Android app for the Open Motion project: a browser-class motion graphics engine that covers video, audio, images, text, compositing, animation, effects, timelines, preview, rendering and export.
Because that engine runs on the device's own graphics pipeline,
The engine works in a similar way to
, so timelines and media elements can react to state changes in real time while you edit.
3D space such as X, Y, Z positioning, cameras, parallax and three-dimensional rotation, plus low-level APIs for
GPU rendering and custom GLSL shaders
The app is not meant to be just another video editor. It is built to grow into a
The engine is the multimedia foundation of EditorsHub
, handling timelines, video/audio decoding, playback, compositing, animation, effects, filters, GPU rendering, video export, and the 3D and camera systems.
With that engine in place, EditorsHub does not have to rebuild an entire multimedia stack from scratch, and development can focus on what makes the app its own:
the editor UI, keyframes, the timeline, animation workflow, tools, effects and other creative features.

The engine is built on Kotlin Multiplatform and is designed to run on multiple platforms. Its developer material already covers iPhone, iPad and macOS, while Android and Windows are still in development. Web and backend support are planned.
The Open Motion project is also planned to become
fully open source, and is being prepared for that public release.
The engine may not stay exactly as it is today.
Once the framework is fully released we can judge whether its performance, features, compatibility, licensing and direction fit the needs of EditorsHub.
For now, EditorsHub keeps growing as a hands-on project while features and ideas are explored.
Thank you for trying EditorsHub and following it from this early stage.
